text:
maria: starting a canary rollout for vision-encoder v0.10.3 to eu-west-1, GitOps sync kicked off. will shift 10% -> 50% over 5m window. @oncall please watch GPU allocation :eyes:
ci-bot: argo-rollouts: started rollouts/vision-encoder (canary) - weight 10% -> schedule in 60s
devin: seeing spike in 5xxs and some pods Pending with "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu". error logs: 
```
kubectl get pods -n inference | grep vision-encoder
vision-encoder-canary-7f8d9   Pending   0/1   Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
vision-encoder-rc-xxxxx       Running   1/1
```
ash: rollback? we can abort the traffic shift and rollback to stable via Argo. but we should avoid manual rollbacks if we can fix capacity quickly.
sam: quick mitigation -> scale node pool/gpu-pool autoscaler up, but that's TF change for GCE/AKS/eks. example for GKE node pool terraform snippet: 
```
resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu_pool" {
  name       = "gpu-pool"
  autoscaling {
    min_node_count = 1
    max_node_count = 10
  }
  node_config {
    accelerator {
      type  = "nvidia-tesla-t4"
      count = 1
    }
  }
}
```
lee: cost note — jumping max_node_count to 10 might double monthly spend for this region. prefer an ephemeral burst via preemptible/spot GPUs if okay. recommend patch: max_node_count -> 3 for now and monitor.
oncall-bot: incident #INC-2025-071 created for canary failure (assigned: @devin).
devops: root cause is we didn't guard the rollout with a cluster-capacity preflight. proposal: add two things to GitOps pipeline:
- a pre-deploy job that runs a quick capacity check script
- an automated rollback policy in Argo Rollouts based on error rate/latency thresholds and missing resource events
Example preflight check (ci job): 
```
#!/bin/bash
REQUIRED_GPUS=2
AVAILABLE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.allocatable.nvidia\.com/gpu}' | tr ' ' '\n' | paste -sd+ - | bc)
if [ "$AVAILABLE" -lt "$REQUIRED_GPUS" ]; then
  echo "not enough GPUs: $AVAILABLE available"
  exit 1
fi
```
devops: and Argo Rollouts can enforce progressive weights + analysis. example (simplified):
```
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
spec:
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 5
      - pause: {duration: 5m}
      - setWeight: 25
      - pause: {duration: 10m}
      - setWeight: 50
  analysis:
    templates:
    - templateName: error-rate-check
```
ash: immediate steps I took: halted the rollout via Argo UI (paused), promoted stable back to 100% traffic. opening PR to bump gpu-pool max -> 3 and add the preflight job + small Argo policy to abort on "Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" events.
maria: thanks. can we also add these checks to the infra CI job that runs on every TF apply? we need lint + a plan-time check that warns if a rollout references GPUs in a region with <2 available GPUs (region constraints).
lee: I'll draft a cheap plan-run script that queries provider for available GPU quotas/regions and fail the TF apply with a warning. we should also document cost tradeoffs in the PR.
devin: assigning follow-ups: @sam codify node pool change PR, @lee add quota check script PR, @devops add preflight + rollout analysis PR. I'll keep incident open until metrics stabilize.
maria: also add an alert runbook: if canary errors > 0.5% for 3m or pods Pending due to GPU for >2m -> auto-abort rollout + tag infra-oncall.
oncall-bot: @devin assigned incident #INC-2025-071 to devin.
nash: ack. working on the Argo analysis template now. will share soon. :thumbsup:
sam: PR opened: terraform: bump gpu_pool max_node_count=3, adding label for spot-burst capability. link: https://git.redwood.dev/infra/merge/123
maria: great. once PRs are up, let's add a short postmortem note in #postmortems with timeline and actions. thanks everyone.
